items.title: EXCLUSIVE: India's ₹500 Crore Space Insurance Cap Leaves Private Sector Exposed | Front Page
items.summary:
India's private space economy is expanding rapidly, with companies like Agnikul, Skyroot, Pixxel, and Galaxeye building orbital launch vehicles and satellite constellations. However, under the 1972 Liability Convention, the Indian government remains strictly liable for damages caused by space objects launched from its territory, even if operated by private entities. To address this exposure, IN-SPACe has proposed mandating third-party liability insurance capped at ₹500 crore ($60M+). But with global reinsurance premiums volatile and catastrophic risks easily exceeding ₹500 crore, can Indian space startups afford the cost of compliance?

In this episode of Front Page, Antara Gupta sits down with Eshaan Bansal, Legal Counsel & Research Fellow at Spaceport SARABHAI, to break down the global space insurance landscape. They discuss international liability frameworks, maximum probable loss (MPL) calculations, why mission insurance is more expensive than third-party cover, establishing a domestic nuclear-style insurance pool or catastrophe bond structure in Gift City, and managing orbital debris risks.

How can India protect taxpayers without pricing its emerging space startups out of orbit?

items.title: EXCLUSIVE: MWire Labs Unveils Lemka AI for Northeast India
items.summary:
Operating out of Shillong, Meghalaya, a six-person team at MWire Labs has built more foundational AI models for Northeast India’s languages than most heavily funded research labs in the country. Within a year of launching, the team has released NE-BERT (a multilingual model outperforming mBERT on regional dialects), Kren-M (a Khasi-English conversational model based on Gemma 2), and Lemka (a full speech-to-text and text-to-speech system for six Northeast languages built on 1,000+ hours of custom field audio).

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Badal Nyalang, Director & Researcher at MWire Labs, to break down how grassroots AI is being built. They discuss field audio collection across remote tribal villages, managing consent and cultural preservation, deploying offline AI prototypes for low-connectivity hill terrains, and ranking 18th on India's national AIKosh repository ahead of major institutions.

Can hyper-local, bootstrapped research labs drive true linguistic sovereignty for India's 200+ underrepresented dialects?

items.title: How to Choose Model Size and Effort Level: The Two Critical Dials (Ep. 1020 with Jon Krohn)
items.summary:
In Episode #1020, @JonKrohnLearns unpacks the two dials that increasingly decide what you get out of a large language model: which model size you pick and how much effort you tell it to spend. Using a July Anthropic blog post by Claude Code’s Lydia Holly as a jumping-off point, with guidance that generalizes to any model family, Jon explains what each setting actually does under the hood. Model size swaps which frozen weights handle your request (roughly, how capable), while effort sets how thorough and certain the model must be before calling a task done, not a simple “thinking-time slider.” He offers a clean diagnostic for when to raise effort versus move to a bigger model, shows why cheaper-per-token isn’t always cheaper-per-task and surveys how OpenAI, Google and open-weight labs have all converged on these same two dials.

In this episode you will learn:
• (00:00) Introduction
• (00:56) What the model-size dial actually does
• (05:29) Why effort isn’t a thinking-time slider
• (13:25) Three practical takeaways for using both dials

Additional materials: https://www.superdatascience.com/1020
